ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Preventive Visit — Booker T. Washington — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

text.paragraph: Periodic preventive visit; no new complaints. [S]

Mr. Washington comes for his periodic preventive visit. He completed the health risk assessment before the visit. The back strain from August cleared in about ten days with heat, walking, and acetaminophen, and he has taken no NSAIDs since. His home blood pressures over the past two weeks have averaged in the low 120s systolic. His headaches have not returned and his concentration is better than in the spring, although he still tires by evening on travel days. He has had no emergency visits or hospital stays. He takes his four blood pressure and kidney medicines and his statin from a weekly organizer and has added no over-the-counter medicines or supplements. [S]

Periodic preventive visit, age 59. Health risk assessment reviewed and a written prevention plan given. Depression and alcohol screens are negative. His kidney disease shapes several preventive choices: vaccines, the colonoscopy preparation, and avoiding NSAIDs. [S]
Next preventive visit in one year.

Severe hypertension with hypertensive kidney disease (I12.9). Blood pressure 122/76 mmHg, below 130/80 and close to the KDIGO systolic target below 120 when tolerated; no orthostatic symptoms. [S]
Continue amlodipine, losartan, and chlorthalidone; standardized office reading at the six-month review in October.

Chronic kidney disease stage G3b A3 (N18.32). eGFR 30 in August, stable; UACR 360 mg/g in June, down from 820. [S]
Continue losartan and dapagliflozin.
eGFR, UACR, hemoglobin, calcium, phosphate, PTH, and the kidney failure risk score at the October review, on the CMID schedule.

Hyperlipidemia (E78.5). On moderate-intensity atorvastatin, as recommended for adults 50 and older with chronic kidney disease. [S]
Continue atorvastatin 20 mg; no repeat LDL, per KDIGO.

Hypertensive retinopathy, both eyes (H35.033). Unchanged on undilated funduscopy; no symptoms. [S]
Next dilated eye examination in May.

Follow-up: Colonoscopy referral sent; PSA and hepatitis C and HIV screening with the October blood draw. Zoster vaccine dose 2 in two to six months. Six-month blood pressure and kidney review in October. Next preventive visit in one year. Next scheduled visit 1915-10-26: six-month blood pressure and chronic kidney disease review. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 20 minutes, with his consent, prompted by his chronic kidney disease. He has named a health care agent and has a written health care directive; a copy is now in the chart. He wants full treatment for reversible illness, including hospital care. He asked to learn more about the options if his kidney function falls further, including dialysis and conservative care, and that discussion will continue with nephrology. He will review these wishes with his agent. [S]
